name: band-signup-form
description: Sign-up band with an address check: a single-column form (name, e-mail, one choice that shapes what is sent, consent, an opt-in) that writes a record, then a verification step that confirms the address and says what happens next. It runs AFTER the platform sign-in when the app has accounts, or on its own for a letter or a list a visitor joins.
provenPattern: The sign-up-with-verification band: ask the least the list needs, write it, confirm the address with a six-digit code, then say it worked.

knowledge.purpose: Joining something with a verified address: the form asks only what the list uses, writes one record through the app's entity, and on success swaps itself for a verification card with its own code form; a valid code swaps that for a confirmation. Sign-in and sign-up of an ACCOUNT are the platform's screens; this band is the app's own list or profile step, never its login door
useCases: A newsletter or letter sign-up with a confirmed e-mail address
Event or waitlist registration with an address check
A first-run profile step after the platform sign-in
antiPatterns: Using it as the app's sign-up or sign-in form — the platform owns that screen once the app requires sign-in; a page form that posts to /auth/login or asks for a password is a gate finding
Asking for more than the list needs — a date of birth on a letter sign-up is a drop-off and a privacy cost
Showing the verification step before the record is written — it is revealed by {{state.signupSent}}, not laid out in advance
A verification step that answers nothing — a valid code always ends on the confirmation
Two sign-up bands on one page
A code step the app cannot check — a form that accepts any six digits is a pretend verification; confirm what was really written

One failure line for every refusal — the failure copy follows the write's reason (statusKeys.reason → {{state.signupReason}}: validation, unauthenticated, forbidden, conflict, network, server or error): the page's words for that reason, held in {{state.signupCopy}}, else the generic failure copy; the refused field names are in {{state.signupFields}}. The server's own words are never shown
A result nobody notices — the result (done or failed) takes focus when it appears

mobileCollapse: Already single-column; the form stretches to the viewport width, the verification card and the confirmation take its place.

placeholders.{{TITLE}}: band heading — what this step completes, in the app language
placeholders.{{SUBTITLE}}: one sentence under the heading: why these details are asked for
placeholders.{{ENTITY}}: the app’s entity type a sign-up is written to (e.g. Subscriber) — its fields take the form’s names: name, email, role, terms, newsletter
placeholders.{{SUBMIT_LABEL}}: label of the profile submit button, in the app language
placeholders.{{NAME_LABEL}}: label of the full-name field, in the app language
placeholders.{{EMAIL_LABEL}}: label of the contact e-mail field, in the app language
placeholders.{{ROLE_LABEL}}: label of the one choice that shapes what is sent (e.g. What do you do?), in the app language
placeholders.{{ROLE_PLACEHOLDER}}: the empty choice shown before a role is picked (e.g. "Choose one")
placeholders.{{ROLE_OPTIONS}}: the roles this app really has: [{label, value}] — labels in the app language, values stable ids; never invent roles
placeholders.{{TERMS_LABEL}}: consent checkbox label — ONE obligation, naming what is stored and why; the box is required
placeholders.{{NEWSLETTER_LABEL}}: newsletter toggle label — what the visitor opts in to
placeholders.{{DONE_TEXT}}: the confirmation once the sign-up is written — what happens next and when (e.g. The first letter arrives on Sunday.)
placeholders.{{FAILED_TEXT}}: alert title when the sign-up could not be written and no copy for its reason is given, in the visitor’s words (e.g. Your sign-up did not arrive — send it again); plain text. The server’s own reason is never shown

{{FAILED_VALIDATION}}.description: the failure copy when the server refused one or more fields (400) — the refused field names are in {{state.signupFields}}, in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_UNAUTHENTICATED}}.description: the failure copy when the visitor is not signed in (401), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_FORBIDDEN}}.description: the failure copy when the visitor may not write this (403), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_CONFLICT}}.description: the failure copy when the record already exists (409, a unique field) — e.g. "You are already on the list", in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_NETWORK}}.description: the failure copy when nothing reached the server (no connection), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_SERVER}}.description: the failure copy when the server failed (5xx), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown
